sentences.text: Shri Tuljesh Goyal, learned counsel for the applicant  Ms. Mradula Sen, learned Govt. Advocate for the respo  ORDER 1.

This is second application filed by the applicant under Section 4 83 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, for grant of bail in connection with Crime No.126/2024 dated (not mentioned), registered at Police Station-Bediya, District-Khargone for the offence under Sections 363, 366-A, 376, 376(3), 376(2)(n) & 344 of IPC, 1860 and Section 3/4 of POCSO Act.
The applicant is in custody since 12.12.2024.
2. It is matter of bail jump.
3. Learned counsel for the applicant submits that the applicant was granted bail and applicant was regularly appearing before the learned trial Court on 31.07.2024.
Thereafter, arrest warrant was issued against the applicant and he was arrested on 12.12.2024.
Since then he is in custody.

Learned counsel for applicant submits that the applicant is a labour and went outside from his hometown due to which he could not appear before the NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:725 2 MCRC-831-2025 Court on 14.11.2024.
He further assures that the applicant will not abscond further and also will regularly appear before the trial Court and comply with all the conditions imposed by this Court.
4. Learned Panel Lawyer for the State opposes the bail application by submitting that it is a case of bail jump.

sentences.text: 5. Looking to the facts and circumstances of the case and the arguments advanced by the learned counsel for the parties and on perusal of the material available on record without commenting on the merits of the case, this application is allowed.

6. It is directed that, the applicant shall be released on bail on furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty thousand only) with two solvent sureties of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty thousand only) each to the satisfaction of the trial Court, to appear before the trial Court on the dates given by the Court.

The applicant shall also abide by the conditions enumerated under Section 480(3) of BNSS.
7.
This order shall be effective till the end of the trial.
However, in case of bail jump and breach of any of the conditions of bail, it shall become ineffective.
Certified copy as per rules.
